questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to experience the Australian lifestyle and culture. Australia is also interesting in terms of my field of study so it was really interesting to see how they do things

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy and the uni staff are very helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were two different orientations. One for all international students which was not that useful and another for just exchange students and that was very helpful and gave you all the info you needed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find but it is a bit expensive. I would recommend Yugo, Switch or Scape. I lived at Dwell which I would not recommend

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can choose to live in a student accommodation in the city which is very convenient for getting to uni and to social things. You can also find roommates for a house outside the city where you can get a pool for around the same price but be aware that the transport is not easy if your going out on the weekend and you will have to take expensive ubers

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to get accepted to the courses and then I could choose which tutorials I wanted to go to

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, they have a system where you can put different tutorials in and see how the schedule turns out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One of the courses I wanted was full but I got one very similar to it. All the other courses I got into no problem

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be early so you can get the courses you want and make the best schedule

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall the level is pretty much the same however it is a lot easier to pass as assignements and participation counts toward your grade

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. They record the lectures so most people watch from home and only come to the tutorials, so that makes the lectures a bit less interactive

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Game Theory
Public Economics
International Trade and Investment Policy
Business Valuation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on what you're after. I thought Game Theory was a lot harder than the other courses but it was also by far the one where i learned the most. I would recommend that if you're willing to put in the work. International Trade was also a nice course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Getting the visa has a surprisingly high fee, otherwise it was mostly as I had expected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some things are cheaper and other more expensive. Housing is a bit more expensive as the student accomodations are privately run and cater mostly to international students. So it is more focused on making money than a "kollegie" in Denmark. Some food types are cheaper than expected. There are a lot of places doing take away sushi were you can get it relatively cheaply. Alcohol is a lot more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many things, like sports, sailing, rockclimbing, waterskiing etc. Just make sure to check them out early so you get your worth from the membership fee

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend some of the outdoor activities. There are also some parties put on through the uni, but they are a bit hit and miss with some being really fun and others not being.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Far North Queensland is the best place i've ever been.
Uluru is also very nice. Do yourself the favour of staying outdoors in a swag if you go. Don't be scared of snakes and spiders.
There are some really nice sport down the Flereau peninsula and Kangaroo Island(Ferry is expensive tho).
A wine trip to the Mclaren Vale is a must.
In general the Adelaide Hills have a lot of nice spots, go and see some koalas

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Aussies are very welcoming and friendly. Them speaking English also makes it a lot easier to get to know people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just try and talk to people. I ended up becoming good friends with some guys from my class just because we randomly sat down at the same table on the first day and started talking. So just start talking to people

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are not as punctual which can be a bit difficult when you are from Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and laid back vibe. Everyone is just so friendly and easy to talk to. I got a lot more integrated in the local culture than I think people do in other exchange destinations.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find out early what clubs you want to join so you can make the most of it.
Try to talk to local aussies not just other internationals.
Go out and explore the area in your free time, you can get to a lot of nice places by bus or train

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Uni Adelaide and UniSA are merging right now so make sure the info you have is up to date

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the people and integrating myself in the culture. I have met some wonderful people and had the experience of living on the other side of the globe

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me it was that all the friends I made down there are pretty hard to see in person now. It is a bit harder saying goodbye than if you were just staying in a country 3 hours away.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I had a great semester in Adelaide and would highly recommend it

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
